node-1.label: 17-year-old male with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions

node-2.label: One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved; he denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms.

node-3.label: He took acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before onset of the mucocutaneous eruption.

node-4.label: Physical examination showed afebrile status, normal vital signs including respiratory rate 16 breaths/min and oxygen saturation 97%; shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate; circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis; 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities; remainder of mucocutaneous (including palms and soles), cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations were unremarkable.

why.why: The transient anosmia/ageusia prodrome, mucocutaneous erosions with scattered vesicles, absence of culprit medication before onset, repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid, and negative Mycoplasma/other respiratory pathogen tests converge on a viral mucocutaneous syndrome. Both laboratory and pathology expert analyses independently reinforce this interpretation and state that all available clinical and imaging information has been reviewed; the sole remaining gap is the pending HSV/VZV/enterovirus PCR/serology and skin biopsy DIF, which prevents complete exclusion of other causes. Confidence is therefore raised to 0.85.

No culprit medication preceded the eruption, and expert analyses agree with the treating team that repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid with negative Mycoplasma/other respiratory pathogens provides a clear viral explanation for the mucocutaneous lesions. Drug-related hypersensitivity is therefore very unlikely, and confidence is lowered to 0.03.

Oral/genital erosions and vesicles remain compatible with autoimmune bullous disease, and skin biopsy DIF is still pending, so it cannot be fully excluded. However, laboratory and pathology expert analyses consistently favor COVID-19-associated mucocutaneous syndrome given the viral prodrome and repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid; this reduces the likelihood of autoimmune bullous disease. Confidence is lowered to 0.15.

node-9.label: Mycoplasma and other respiratory pathogen tests were negative

node-10.label: HSV and enterovirus PCR/serology and skin biopsy direct immunofluorescence results are not yet available
